dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: pṛṣṭhaśūnyaṃ mūlaśūnyaṃ yugapad bhāvayec ca yaḥ | śarīranirapekṣiṇyā śaktyā śūnyamanā bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 44: GRETIL reads pṛṣṭa- ('asked'); corrected to pṛṣṭha- ('back / top') with Wallis, Pradīpaka and Singh. Singh takes pṛṣṭhaśūnya as 'the void above'; Wallis titles the verse 'space above and below'.
dharana.rendering: Whoever contemplates at the same moment the void above and the void at the root becomes, through the power that does not depend on the body, void-minded.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh takes pṛṣṭhaśūnya as 'the void above' and glosses 'the energy independent of the body' as prāṇaśakti; 'void-minded' means free of all thought-constructs. Wallis: the space above, at the crown of the head, and the space at the root of the body. The word pṛṣṭha can also mean 'back'; all three translators consulted read it as 'above'.
dharana.technique_name: The Void Above and the Void at the Base
dharana.instruction: Feel open space above the head and at the base of the body at the same time.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: verse 44: Space above and below (Y18 ~ A2)

source_disagreements: pṛṣṭha: GRETIL's pṛṣṭa ('asked') is an input error; Singh, Wallis and Bäumer read pṛṣṭha and take it as 'above'. The word can also mean 'back'.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 44 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: void above (commentarial: at or above the crown)
void at the base (commentarial: root of the trunk)
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is two open spaces on the vertical line of the body, one above and one at the base, held at the same moment.
geometry.svg_hint: a vertical line with an open circle above the head and an open circle at the base, both highlighted together
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Two ends open
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the two ends of the body's line open at once and the mind between them empties. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Hold the space above and the space at the base together
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The void above and the void at the base, held simultaneously
attention.secondary: The mind between them becoming quiet

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Whoever contemplates at the same moment the void above and the void at the root becomes, through the power that does not depend on the body, void-minded.
adiyogi.method_summary: Feel an open space above the head and an open space at the base of the trunk, both at the same moment. Do not alternate between them. Rest as the mind between them grows empty.

honesty.disclosure: Door 021 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 21 (verse 44) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 021 is dharana 21, verse 44. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Keep the attention light; there is nothing to push or lift. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 021: the void above and the void at the base. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 21, verse 44.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit or lie down. The map is two open spaces on the body's line: one above, one at the base.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor or the chair carry you. Eyes closed or soft.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Feel the space above the head and the space at the base together, at the same moment. Not one, then the other.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: both ends of a line opening at once. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 44: contemplate the void above and the void at the base together, and by a power that does not depend on the body the mind becomes void.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Release the attention. Feel the weight of the body on its support. Open the eyes when ready.
